label: rem:blackwell
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:blackwell}
  The proof generates the attaining coupling from the single Gaussian experiment $Z^\star$ through the Markov chains $M-Z^\star-X^\star$ and $M-Z^\star-Y^\star$, with $(M,X^\star)\overset{d}{=}(M,X)$ and $(M,Y^\star)\overset{d}{=}(M,Y)$. In the language of the comparison of experiments \citep{blackwell1953}, $Z^\star$ is thus at least as informative about $M$ as each source, i.e., a common refinement of $X$ and $Y$ in the sense of \citet{kolchinsky2022novel}. Among Gaussian experiments with this property, $Z^\star$ is the least informative about $M$: any such $Z$ yields, by the same construction, a compatible coupling $Q_Z\in\Delta(P)$ with $I(M;Z)\geq I_{Q_Z}(M;X,Y)\geq\frac12\log_2(\det\Sigma_M/\det\Gamma^\star)=I(M;Z^\star)$, by the data-processing inequality~\eqref{eq:data-processing} and \cref{prop:broja-lower-bound}.

label: lem:info-lower-bound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:info-lower-bound}
  Let
  \[
    M\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu_M,\Sigma_M),
    \qquad
    \Sigma_M\succ0,
  \]
  and let $Z$ be any experiment about $M$, such that $\bar{\Gamma}_Z\succ0$. Then
  \begin{equation}
    I(M;Z)
    \geq
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Sigma_M}{\det\bar{\Gamma}_Z}.
    \label{eq:posterior-error-information-bound}
  \end{equation}

body_md: The kernel~\eqref{eq:garbling-G-S} factors through the sufficient statistic $T_Z := H_Z^\top R_Z^{-1}(Z - \mu_Z)$, which satisfies $T_Z \sim \mathcal{N}(J_Z (M-\mu_M), J_Z)$ conditionally on $M$: since $G(Z - \mu_Z) = H_A J_Z^{-1} T_Z$, the copy $A'$ is obtained by first forming from $Z$ the unbiased estimate $J_Z^{-1} T_Z$ of $M - \mu_M$, whose conditional covariance is $J_Z^{-1}$, and then passing it through the channel of $A$ with the reduced noise covariance $S = R_A - H_A J_Z^{-1} H_A^\top$.

name: Two-stage interpretation

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $Q\in\Delta(P)$ and regard the pair of sources $(X,Y)$, with joint law $Q$, as a single experiment about $M$. Denote by $\bar{\Gamma}^{Q}_{XY}$ its average posterior-error covariance, as defined in Equation~\eqref{eq:average-posterior-error}.

  Since $X$ is a coordinate of $(X,Y)$, the Markov chain
  \[
    M-(X,Y)-X
  \]
  holds under $Q$. Moreover, $Q_{MX}=P_{MX}$ by~\cref{def:compatible-couplings}, and $(M,X)$ is jointly Gaussian under $P_{MX}$ by \cref{ass:gaussian-marginals}, so the average posterior-error covariance of $X$ under $Q$ equals $\Gamma_X$. \cref{lem:posterior-mse} therefore gives
  \[
    \bar{\Gamma}^{Q}_{XY}\preceq\Gamma_X.
  \]
  The same argument with the roles of $X$ and $Y$ interchanged gives
  \[
    \bar{\Gamma}^{Q}_{XY}\preceq\Gamma_Y.
  \]

  If $I_Q(M;X,Y)=+\infty$, the claimed inequality is immediate. Otherwise $h(M\mid X,Y)>-\infty$, which forces $\bar{\Gamma}^{Q}_{XY}\succ0$: if $\bar{\Gamma}^{Q}_{XY}$ were singular, the error vector $M-\mathbb{E}_Q[M\mid X,Y]$ would be supported on a proper subspace, so that $h(M\mid X,Y)\leq h(M-\mathbb{E}_Q[M\mid X,Y])=-\infty$. Hence $\bar{\Gamma}^{Q}_{XY}\in\mathcal{F}_{X,Y}$, the feasible set in Equation~\eqref{eq:feasible-posterior-covariances}, and the optimality of $\Gamma^\star$ established in \cref{prop:max-det} yields
  \[
    \det\bar{\Gamma}^{Q}_{XY}\leq\det\Gamma^\star.
  \]
  Applying \cref{lem:info-lower-bound} to the experiment $(X,Y)$ and then this determinant inequality,
  \[
    I_Q(M;X,Y)
    \geq
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Sigma_M}{\det\bar{\Gamma}^{Q}_{XY}}
    \geq
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Sigma_M}{\det\Gamma^\star}.
  \]
  Since $Q\in\Delta(P)$ was arbitrary, taking the infimum over $\Delta(P)$ in the definition~\eqref{eq:broja-union} of the BROJA union information proves Equation~\eqref{eq:broja-lower-bound}.

title: Proof
body_md:
The BROJA redundancy satisfies
  \[
    \operatorname{RI}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}
    =
    I(M;X)-\operatorname{UI}_X^{\mathrm{BROJA}}.
  \]
  By Equation~\eqref{eq:ui-union-relation} and \cref{thm:gaussian-broja},
  \[
    \operatorname{UI}_X^{\mathrm{BROJA}}
    =
    I_{\cup}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}(M;X,Y)-I(M;Y),
  \]
  so
  \[
    \operatorname{RI}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}
    =
    I(M;X)+I(M;Y)-I_{\cup}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}(M;X,Y).
  \]
  Since $(M,X)$ and $(M,Y)$ are jointly Gaussian,
  \[
    I(M;X)
    =
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Sigma_M}{\det\Gamma_X},
    \qquad
    I(M;Y)
    =
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Sigma_M}{\det\Gamma_Y}.
  \]
  \cref{thm:gaussian-broja} gives
  \[
    I_{\cup}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}(M;X,Y)
    =
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Sigma_M}{\det\Gamma^\star}.
  \]
  Substituting these three expressions yields
  \[
    \operatorname{RI}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}
    =
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Sigma_M\,\det\Gamma^\star}
    {\det\Gamma_X\,\det\Gamma_Y}.
  \]

  For synergy, the BROJA PID identity gives
  \[
    \operatorname{SI}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}
    =
    I(M;X,Y)-I_{\cup}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}(M;X,Y).
  \]
  Because the observed triple $(M,X,Y)$ is jointly Gaussian,
  \[
    I(M;X,Y)
    =
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Sigma_M}{\det\Gamma_{XY}}.
  \]
  Subtracting the union-information formula from \cref{thm:gaussian-broja} therefore gives
  \[
    \operatorname{SI}^{\mathrm{BROJA}}
    =
    \frac12\log_2
    \frac{\det\Gamma^\star}{\det\Gamma_{XY}},
  \]
  which proves the result.
